name: Amok
overview: Amok was a male Levite and a priest, descended from Aaron, who played a role among the priests who returned with Zerubbabel. His identity as a priest highlights his service in the religious life of Israel during the post-exilic period. He is specifically noted in Nehemiah 12:7 as part of the priestly group involved in the restoration of worship in Jerusalem.
namesAndTitles: The name Amok means 'capable' and is a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 12:7. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew personal name within the priestly lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Amok is explicitly identified as a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, establishing his priestly heritage. Additionally, it is inferred that his father was Eber, as noted in Nehemiah 12:20. Beyond these connections, Scripture does not provide further family relationships for Amok.
scriptureSignificance: Amok's significance lies in his role as a priest who returned with Zerubbabel, contributing to the reestablishment of the priesthood and temple worship after the Babylonian exile. His Aaronic descent underscores the continuity of the priestly line during this critical period of restoration, affirming God's faithfulness in preserving the Levitical priesthood. His mention in Nehemiah highlights the importance of faithful service in rebuilding the spiritual foundation of Israel.
